deepseek_v4_pro/001: This strategy uses iterative deepening alpha‑beta search with a heuristic evaluation that considers store difference, total seeds on the board, and mobility. Moves are ordered to prioritize extra turns and captures. The search continues until 0.95 seconds have elapsed, then returns the best move from the deepest fully completed depth.
deepseek_v4_pro/002: The strategy is based on iterative deepening minimax with alpha-beta pruning. The evaluation function uses the store difference plus a small bonus for having more seeds in the player's own houses (to favor mobility and future captures). Moves are ordered heuristically by a quick evaluation of the resulting board to improve prune efficiency. A time limit of ~0.9 seconds per move is enforced, and the best move found within the time is returned. If a timeout occurs during search, the best fully evaluated move from the previous depth is used.
deepseek_v4_pro/003: The strategy uses an iterative deepening minimax search with alpha-beta pruning. A heuristic evaluation function scores non-terminal states by weighting the store difference (×2) plus the difference in seeds in houses. At each node, moves are ordered by evaluating the resulting state to improve pruning efficiency. The search depth increases until a time limit of ~0.95 seconds is reached, ensuring a move is always returned within the allowed 1 second. The best move found in the deepest completed search is selected.
deepseek_v4_pro/004: The strategy is an iterative deepening negamax search with alpha-beta pruning and a transposition table. It uses a simple heuristic (store difference) and move ordering based on a 1-ply static evaluation. The search is time-limited to 0.95 seconds to ensure a legal move is always returned within the arena constraints.
deepseek_v4_pro/005: The strategy uses iterative deepening alpha-beta search. The heuristic evaluation is the final score difference if the game ended immediately (total seeds on our side minus total on opponent's side), which perfectly aligns with the end‑game sweeping rule. Moves are ordered at each node by preferring moves that grant an extra turn, then by the resulting heuristic score. The search runs until 0.95 seconds have elapsed, and the best move from the deepest fully completed iteration is returned.
